subject: Keystone Health streaming: intermittent WebSocket timeouts & elevated error rate
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@keystonehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: support@keystonehealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:12:43 -0700
Subject: [Keystone] Realtime feed: intermittent timeouts and errors during peak windows

Hi Jordan / Grace,

Over the last three production windows (09:00–11:00 PST, 14:00–15:00 PST yesterday), our clinical ingestion pipeline started seeing intermittent WebSocket timeouts and a spike in 5xx errors from the Redwood streaming endpoint. The symptoms:
- Client sessions receive silent gaps (no chunked messages) for ~6–12s, then the connection resets.
- Overall error rate for streaming requests jumped from ~0.2% to ~4.8% during the peak.
- Throughput appears to be throttled: token throughput drops by ~30% for affected sessions.

We attempted a graceful reconnect which helped briefly but the failures return under sustained load. This is impacting our triage assistants during peak hours.

I've attached a short pcap and the dashboard screenshot showing the error spike. Can you confirm whether this is on our side (client keepalive) or something on the Redwood runtime / proxy layer? We need an ETA for a mitigation; if we must fall back to non-streaming API for the afternoon peak we need to know the expected performance impact.

Thanks,
Alex
Account Director, Keystone Health
attachments: keystone_pcap_snippet.gz, streaming-dashboard-0615.png

Alex — thanks for the quick flag. We're treating this as P1 because of the customer impact during peak.

Immediate plan:
1) Marcus and runtime team to triage logs and confirm whether chunked transfer / WS idle timeouts are triggering upstream.
2) Short-term mitigation: if we can confirm this is a proxy/keepalive mismatch, we can (a) increase the proxy keepalive and WS ping interval, or (b) enable a short-lived non-streaming fallback for specific routes for the afternoon peak.
3) I'll open an internal incident and loop in leadership if the mitigation is not possible within 2 hours.

Please share any additional traces (X-Request-ID values, timestamps) — Marcus and I will correlate with logs. We'll also provide an expected performance delta if you fall back to polling/non-streaming.

-Jordan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@keystonehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:02:54 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Keystone] Realtime feed: intermittent timeouts and errors during peak windows

Jordan / Grace / Alex — initial triage notes below after looking at the provided pcap and our edge logs (attached: keystone_logs_20270615.txt):

What I see:
- Multiple client connections show a pattern of small bursts followed by long idle periods; server side marks socket as WRITE_BUFFER_FULL for ~6–10s before the connection is torn down by the upstream proxy with a 504.
- Proxy (edge) is accumulating queued writes when downstream RT kernel wakeups are delayed under high throughput (we're seeing non-linear queuing in the worker queue depth metric).
- There are also intermittent chunk-coalescing delays where the runtime waits to reach a batch threshold; under the current batching policy (adaptive, aggressive for cost) the batch wait can add 50–200ms, which compounds under queueing.
- No obvious application-level exception inside the model runtime — tokens are generated but delivery to socket stalls.

Immediate mitigations I can push now (30–60m):
- Disable adaptive coalescing for Keystone's route (force smaller batching and more frequent flush). This trades some CPU/units for lower tail latency.
- Increase edge proxy keepalive and WS ping grace period to reduce false disconnects (config change at LB).
- Temporarily route Keystone's traffic to a higher-priority pool with lower worker queue depth.

Planned fix (1–2 weeks roadmap):
- Runtime change to implement heartbeat token throughput that flushes KV / chunk buffer on guaranteed intervals (patch ready in branch: feature/heartbeat-flush).
- Improve backpressure signalling between runtime and proxy to avoid long WRITE_BUFFER_FULL states.

I will push a configuration change to disable coalescing for the Keystone route and increase the proxy keepalive (requesting ops change now). I will attach a short snippet of the relevant log lines below for visibility.

--- log excerpt ---
2027-06-15T09:17:03Z [edge-proxy] conn=0x7f3c WRITE_BUFFER_FULL queued=138 latency_ms=9800 route=keystone-realtime
2027-06-15T09:17:04Z [runtime] shard=3 flush_delay_ms=128 batch_wait_ms=162 tokens_pending=48
2027-06-15T09:17:05Z [edge-proxy] conn=0x7f3c upstream=504 route=keystone-realtime x-request-id=KS-REQ-1122
--- end excerpt ---

I'll report back once the config change is active and we have short-term telemetry.

-Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks Marcus — we pushed the afternoon traffic through the adjusted route at ~13:50 PST. The keepalive bump helped some connections, but under sustained user load at 14:05–14:30 we still saw ~3% session resets and a 25% throughput degradation for the assistant endpoint.

Sample client trace (truncated):
---
[14:06:12.102] ws.recv() stalled for 11.3s
[14:06:23.405] connection reset by peer
x-request-id: KS-REQ-1147
---

We are starting to see customer-visible errors and our internal ops are asking for executive visibility. If you expect the planned runtime fix is 1–2 weeks, we need a deterministic workaround for the next 48 hours (either guaranteed route isolation or a config that prevents socket stalls under high concurrency). Please advise — if you recommend fallback to non-streaming polling we need an estimate of the UX hit.

-Alex

Tessa — looping you in. Keystone (strategic HS account) is seeing persistent WebSocket chunk delivery stalls under peak load despite the keepalive/route adjustments Marcus applied. Marcus indicates a runtime/proxy queuing interaction that's causing long WRITE_BUFFER_FULL states which then trigger upstream 504s. Short-term config tweaks helped but didn't eliminate customer-visible resets.

Requested actions:
- Approve routing Keystone to an isolated high-priority pool for 48 hours while Marcus verifies whether route isolation removes the failure class. This will consume reserved capacity but should be a fast mitigation.
- Confirm whether we should offer a one-off SLA credit if we do not return to <0.5% streaming error rate within 72 hours.
- Coordinate a customer-facing update (Alex needs a message within 90 minutes).

Thanks all — keep me posted in the incident thread.
